# Percussion Loan Store Procedure

Fictional Cedar Lantern Dance Studio. Training fixture only; no real studio policy.

## What the loan store provides
The studio lends small hand drums, frame drums and practice pads for enrolled rhythm classes. Loan instruments are teaching equipment, not personal gifts. A label on the case identifies the asset number, kit contents and inspection date. A student borrows the entire listed kit so that the return can be checked against a clear inventory. A strap found loose in a room is not added to a kit without recording it.

A standard percussion instrument loan lasts 21 calendar days from the signed collection date. The collection day is day zero and the due date is written on the receipt. A student may return earlier without a fee. Returning the case to a teaching room is not a completed return; the store desk must inspect and acknowledge it. The receipt remains the reference if the timetable changes during the loan.

An enrolled student must reserve a loan instrument at least three business days before collection. A reservation names the intended class and required instrument size. The store may offer a practice pad when the requested drum is unavailable, but the student can decline that substitute. A teacher keeping equipment for a studio-led rehearsal uses the departmental checkout list instead of a student loan.

## Deposit and unresolved checklist difference
The store procedure requires a 45 dollar refundable deposit for a hand-drum kit. The repair desk checklist lists a different refundable deposit for the same hand-drum kit. Both instructions are active and neither declares precedence. Staff must preserve both amounts in an answer and request clarification; this is not permission to collect two deposits. A frame-drum repair estimate or a lesson fee should not be used to resolve the difference.

## Caring for borrowed equipment
Borrowed percussion must be carried inside its closed case whenever it is outdoors, including in dry weather. The purpose is to protect tension fittings and prevent straps catching on doors. A case should not be left in a hot car or against a heater. If the drum gets wet, stop using it and contact the store before attempting to tighten the skin. Household oil, glue and adhesive tape are not approved repairs.

Hands should be clean and dry before practice. Keep drinks off the same table and allow the instrument to reach room temperature before opening a cold case. Use the supplied soft cloth for the shell only; a damp cloth suitable for a plastic practice pad may damage another surface. Store staff demonstrate the correct handling at collection and can repeat the explanation without extending the loan automatically.

## Renewal and recall
A loan can be renewed once for seven days if no other student has reserved that asset. Renewal must be confirmed by the store before the existing due date. A message sent after the desk closes does not itself approve the extension. The repair desk can recall an instrument that develops a safety fault even when a normal renewal would otherwise be available; follow the repair notice rather than assuming the original due date is guaranteed.

## Collection and identity
A guardian may collect for a younger student if the booking records their name. The desk checks the collection record and shows the kit before obtaining a signature. Do not ask another student to take an unsealed kit home as a favour. A classmate can carry an empty spare case during a supervised rehearsal, but that does not transfer the loan responsibility.

## Stock count and a practical example
At the weekly stock count, the clerk compares every case number with its contents. A missing beater is recorded separately from a damaged drumhead. For example, Tali returns kit H-14 with its two beaters and strap but reports a new rattle. The clerk marks the report, isolates the kit for inspection and gives Tali a written acknowledgement. The store does not make Tali diagnose the fault before accepting the return. Questions about the deposit remain open until the store and repair desk reconcile their current instructions; a fault report is not an excuse to choose a convenient amount.

## Cross-campus closing procedure

A transfer between campuses is a move of a loan asset and should leave a clear trail even when the student who will borrow it has not yet arrived. The sending clerk checks the case number against the stock list and opens the case on a clear desk. Check that each beater is present and that the strap lies inside the case rather than across the hinge. Write down any mark already seen on the shell so that the next clerk does not mistake it for new damage. Close the lid and test the latch without putting weight on the drum. If the case has a loose hinge, use another inspected case and record both case numbers. The asset tag stays with the instrument and is not peeled off to make the case look tidy. A driver taking several kits reads the labels aloud with the sending clerk before loading. Put the heavier cases on the floor of the vehicle and keep them clear of loose chairs or bags. Do not stack a box of office files on top of a drum case merely because the lid looks flat. The receiving site should know which vehicle is coming and which adult will bring the equipment to the desk. An estimated arrival time is useful for planning but is not a proof that the instrument has been received. If the driver is delayed, tell the receiving clerk rather than leaving the cases outside a locked door. A student waiting for the drum can use a studio practice pad while staff arrange the actual handover. The student does not need to wait by the loading bay or contact the driver directly. When the kits reach the other campus, the receiving clerk checks each asset label before opening a case. Compare the contents with the sending note and inspect the strap and beaters again. A new rattle or a missing item is recorded at once so that the next lesson does not begin with an unexplained fault. Keep the transfer paperwork with the desk record rather than placing it loose inside a student's bag. The receiving clerk may ask the sending clerk to clarify a mark, but the student is not asked to settle a disagreement between sites. If the case is cold from the trip, let it reach room temperature before opening it for practice. A loan can be reserved before transfer, yet a reservation does not mean that the student has collected the item. Staff should distinguish the transport time from the period in the student's care. The driver returning an empty vehicle is not evidence that every kit was accepted at the other desk. Before closing the transfer task, compare the number of cases loaded with the number accepted. Any difference remains open until someone locates the asset and records the handover. A clerk who leaves at the end of a shift tells the next clerk which kits still need checking. The next clerk uses the same record rather than starting a new loan in order to clear a queue. The final step is the specific receiving signature rule stated at the end of this paragraph. For an instrument sent between campuses, the receiving clerk must sign the amber transfer card before the loan clock starts.

## Labels and similar equipment
A practice pad with a black rim and a frame drum with a black case can look similar at a distance. The clerk reads the asset label rather than relying on colour. The same applies when two kits have matching straps. A temporary paper label may point out a loose latch, but it must not obscure the permanent asset number. A student who finds an unfamiliar beater in their case reports it to the desk; staff compare the kit lists before changing an inventory. An honest discrepancy report is not automatically a damage claim.

## A loan during a timetable change
If a rhythm class moves from Tuesday to Thursday, the loan receipt retains its recorded due date unless the desk confirms a renewal. The teacher can help the family contact the store but cannot silently change the stock system by writing a later date on the class board. For a student missing a week through illness, the family should ask about safe return or a permitted extension. The store does not infer eligibility from a class absence, and the original equipment remains traceable while the request is considered.
